newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat as market awaits G7.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat as market awaits G7.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished steady on Friday after being stuck in a tight 200-point range with interest subdued ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) summit due to start later in the day.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended five points higher at 20,460 after touching an early peak of 20,580 on listless volume of 9,108 lots.
"Even the small traders are talking about the G7," a trader with a local futures house said.
He said news U.S. President Bill Clinton had voiced concern to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about Japan's rising trade surplus weighed on the market early in the day.
Dealers said the market was likely to remain in its current 20,300-20,800 range ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan business sentiment survey, due on June 25.
The September Nikkei was expected to remain well supported around 20,200-20,300, while the 20,750 level would pose a stiff barrier, the trader said.
Taiwan futures ended sharply higher as the underlying cash market ended at a seven-year high on strong gains in the financial and electronic sectors.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 379.7 on volume of 1,397 lots. July settled at 378.1 against an opening 367.5 on volume of 720 lots.
"Buyers tightened their grip on the market when the discount widened to 8.5 points as the cash market broke new highs during the session," Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily market commentary.
It said traders were turning wary of continuing to hold heavy long positions in fear of possible intervention by the Taiwan government to cool the speculative element in the current bull run.
